settings.name_in_paper: (epsilon, delta)-PAC coarse ranking with Bernoulli arms
unmapped: Goal: partition arms into c ordered clusters of pre-specified sizes given by boundaries kappa_1<...<kappa_c=K (coarse ranking), with error tolerance epsilon
the learner knows the cluster boundaries kappa_i and the tolerance epsilon
pairwise-comparison feedback can be handled via Borda reduction (Bernoulli rewards with Borda-score means)
settings.definition_quote: Consider a multi-armed bandit with $K$ arms. Each arm $a$ corresponds to a Bernoulli distribution with an unknown mean $p_a$ ... we say the algorithm is $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PAC if $\P ( \exists \,i \text{ such that }\hat{M}_i \not\subseteq M^\ast_{i,\epsilon}) \le \delta$.

settings.name_in_paper: delta-PAC coarse ranking on separable class M_kappa (lower bound)
unmapped: Goal: exact coarse ranking into clusters with known boundaries kappa_i (epsilon = 0)
arm distributions from a family P with finite positive KL between distinct members satisfying a continuity assumption (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the following class of bandit models where the clusters are unambiguously separated, i.e. $\mathcal{M}_\kappa = \{p = (p_1,\dots,p_K): p_{i} \in \mathcal{P}, p_{\kappa_i} > p_{\kappa_i+1}, 1 \le i < c\}$

symbols.alpha_exp: exponent alpha > 1 in the exploration rate

tuning: beta(t,delta) = log(k_1 K t^alpha/delta) + log log(k_1 K t^alpha/delta)

source.label: thm:pacguarantee
source.quote: $\lucbrank$ using $\beta(t,\delta) = \log(\tfrac{k_1 K t^\alpha}{\delta}) + \log \log (\tfrac{k_1 K t^\alpha}{\delta})$ with $\alpha > 1$ and $k_1 > \left( \frac{c-1}{2} \right)^\alpha + \tfrac{2e}{\alpha-1} + \tfrac{4e}{(\alpha-1)^2}$, is correct with probability $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Correctness (delta-PAC) guarantee: probability of an incorrect (epsilon-tolerant) clustering is at most delta. Appendix restatement uses k_1 > 1 + ... instead.

symbols.H_star: H*_{eps,b} = sum over arms of 1/max(Delta*_b(a), eps^2/2), Delta*_b(a) the Chernoff information between p_a and the nearest boundary point b_i
symbols.C_0: constant with C_0 >= (1+1/e)(alpha log C_0 + 1 + alpha/e)

conditions: b_i in [p_{kappa_i+1}, p_{kappa_i}] arbitrary boundary points
tuning: beta(t,delta) = log(k_1 K t^alpha/delta) + log log(k_1 K t^alpha/delta)

source.label: thm:samplecomplexity
source.quote: Let $\tau$ be the random number of samples taken by $\lucbrank$ before termination. If $\alpha > 1$, \[ \P\left(\tau \le 2C_0(\alpha) H^\ast_{\epsilon,b} \log \left( \frac{k_1 K (2 H^\ast_{\epsilon, b})^\alpha}{\delta} \right)\right) \ge 1-\delta \]

results.notes: Holds with probability >= 1-delta. Tightest bound by minimizing H_star over b.

symbols.Delta_KL_a: KL divergence from arm a to the closest arm of an adjacent cluster (min over adjacent clusters)

conditions: any coarse ranking algorithm that is delta-PAC on M_kappa

source.label: thm:lowerbound
source.quote: Let $p \in \mathcal{M}_\kappa$, and assume that $\mathcal{P}$ satisfies \cref{ass:assumption}; any coarse ranking algorithm that is $\delta$-PAC on $\mathcal{M}_\kappa$ satisfies, for $\delta \le 0.15$, \mathbb{E}_p[\tau] \ge \left[ \sum_{a} \frac{1}{\Delta^{\text{KL}}_\kappa(a)} \right] \log ( \frac{1}{2.4\delta} )

results.notes: Change-of-measure lower bound on expected stopping time.
